message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: ci
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - '**'
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Lint
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Fix usage of insecure GitHub protocol
        run: sudo git config --system url."https://github".insteadOf "git://github"
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Use Node.js 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: 'npm'
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Check Linting
        run: npm run lint

  tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Tests
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Fix usage of insecure GitHub protocol
        run: sudo git config --system url."https://github".insteadOf "git://github"
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Use Node.js 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: 'npm'
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Run Tests
        run: npm test
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true",
  "rationale": "Applied P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout). The measured experiment batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 added timeout-minutes: 5 to a job and reduced median elapsed time from 41s to 30s (26.8% savings) while preserving all checks and successes. This workflow's jobs declare no timeout, and repository history shows successful runs completing in roughly half a minute, so a 5-minute bound is safe headroom that cannot truncate valid runs. All existing steps, triggers, coverage, and concurrency cancellation are preserved; no permissions, secrets, or deployment changes are introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}

But the pattern suggests adding explicit cache. However, the workflow already has cache: 'npm' in setup-node. Hmm.
